title: Royal Óbidos Savages The Back Nine
title_candidates: Royal Óbidos Savages The Back Nine
The Ten-Shot Cushion Becomes A Three-Shot Sweat
Alex Baker's Best Day, Everyone Else's Worst Stretch
theme: Holes 10 to 12 became a killing ground that mauled three different players, yet left both the Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon races exactly where they started — only the Trophy race, undone by Patterson's comedown, actually moved.
tone: Wry, forensic, and quietly delighted by the gap between a scorecard's carnage and its final verdict.
opening_hook: Three players took turns being swallowed whole by holes 10 to 12 at Royal Óbidos, and somehow only one leaderboard noticed.

round_story.subject: Alex Baker's 42-point round is the best of the day and the second-best of his own TEG career, arriving despite a quintuple bogey at the 14th and an eight-shot bleed through holes 10-12.
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the second-best Stableford round of his 11-round TEG history and, at Royal Óbidos specifically, a new course personal best — 102 gross, six shots better than his previous best here and thirteen shots better than his last visit — proof the carnage in the middle of his round didn't actually cost him the day.
round_story.shape: Alex Baker arrived at Royal Óbidos never having broken 108 gross; somewhere in the middle of his round he took a quintuple bogey at the 14th and bled eight shots across holes 10-12, the kind of stretch that usually wrecks a card. Instead he closed with the best Stableford total of the day and a new personal best on the course, the numbers refusing to reflect the chaos that produced them.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Bends But Doesn't Break
round_story.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Bends But Doesn't Break
round_story.standfirst: A quintuple bogey and a three-hole bloodbath through 10-12 somehow still added up to the best Stableford round of the day.

race_story.subject: John Patterson's ten-shot Trophy cushion, built on a near-record 49-point round, shrank to just three after a 34-point comedown at Royal Óbidos.
race_story.why_it_matters: Two separate quadruple bogeys, at the 12th and the 18th, plus a costly early stretch through holes 2-4, turned a laughably comfortable lead into a nervous one with Alex Baker's 42 points closing hard and one round left to play.
race_story.shape: Patterson took a ten-shot Trophy lead into the round on the back of the second-best round in TEG history. A poor 34 at Royal Óbidos — undone by quadruple bogeys at the 12th and 18th and an eight-shot bleed through 2-4 — has cut that cushion to three with the field's best round of the day snapping at his heels.
race_story.standfirst: A pair of quadruple bogeys and a horror start turned a laughably comfortable lead into a nervous one, with a round to go.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker's round split violently in two — a serene front nine undone by a ruinous stretch through holes 10-12.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He piled up 16 points across the first five holes without dropping a gross shot through 1-3, then went three holes without a single net par, bleeding eight shots and taking a quadruple bogey at the 11th — a ten-point front-to-back split that turned a promising round mediocre.
discovered_storylines.shape: Jon Baker's front nine bordered on serene: 16 points in five holes, spotless golf through 1-3. Then holes 10-12 undid all of it — a double bogey, a quadruple bogey, another double, no net pars and eight shots gone. He finished with a 34-point round that flattered to deceive, a microcosm of a topsy-turvy day at Royal Óbidos.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker's Round Of Two Halves
Ten Points Lost In Three Holes
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Jon Baker's Round Of Two Halves
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Sixteen points in five holes gave way to three without a single net par, a swing that summed up the day.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's Green Jacket lead survives a quintuple bogey at the 10th, his worst hole of the tournament so far.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: With Jon Baker seven shots back and this round's chaos elsewhere, the blow-up threatened to hand the initiative straight back, but a tidy start — including a birdie at the 3rd — banked enough that the Jacket gap finished the round exactly where it started.
discovered_storylines.shape: Mullin took a seven-shot Green Jacket cushion into the round. A quintuple bogey at the 10th, his worst hole of the TEG so far, threatened to cut it down. Instead the gap held at seven, unmoved, heading into the final round.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A quintuple bogey at the 10th was as bad as his tournament has been, yet the Jacket gap didn't move an inch.

race_state_note: The Green Jacket gap held at exactly seven and the Wooden Spoon gap crept out by one to fifteen — both leaders unmoved, only the Trophy race sharpened.
